title: 8 · Flash thickness: fill against load
level: Advanced · 3D · built-in die set · ~3–5 min per run
summary: The 1"-8 hex bolt head of demo 4, forged with three flash-land thicknesses within the ASM flash guidance: the classic closed-die trade-off between die fill and press load.
instructions: 1. The die set is the hex bolt head (quarter model, flat and cylindrical die faces, 1 mm edge radius at the flash land). The land runs 1/4" from the hex wall to the gutter (about 5.8 mm flat); its thickness is the input 'Flash land thickness' under Geometry.

2. Run its multi-run: the flash thickness is swept over 1.6, 2.0 and 2.6 mm (1/16" to about 7/64") with the same billet, material and press, so only the flash changes. All three are within industry practice for a 0.3 kg steel forging (ASM survey: about 1.4 mm typical, 0.7–2.8 mm range; land ratio w/t 3.6, 2.9 and 2.2, inside the 2–4 of the handbook load data). The element size is automatic (Balanced, about 8,000 nodes in the quarter model).
3. Compare closing load and final fill in RUNS, or Export ▸ Comparison report for the table and a load / fill chart against flash thickness.
4. A thinner flash chokes the outflow: the pressure in the cavity rises, the hex corners fill, and the load climbs steeply in the last millimetres.
5. A thicker flash lets metal escape: lower load, but the corners may fill later or not at all. Die designers pick the thinnest flash the press can push and the dies can survive.

6. Read the Volume change column too: it should stay within about 2 %. The model is isothermal: in a real press a thin flash chills against the dies and gets stiffer, so the real load rises faster with thinner flash than these runs show. That is why the built-in dies use the thick side of the guidance.
